name: Illinois

statute.readVia: https://web.archive.org/web/20260627233753/https://www.ilga.gov/Documents/legislation/ilcs/documents/062500050K12-503.htm (archived copy of the official ILCS page; ilga.gov unreachable)

windshield.strip: nonreflective tinted film on the uppermost portion, no more than 6 inches down from the top

frontSide.note: 35% (5% variance) only if no window behind the driver is below 35%; 50% film allowed if no rear window is below 30%; 50% if the rear glass is factory-tinted; otherwise no tint on front side windows

backSide.note: no numeric limit in § 12-503, but rear tint below 35% (or 30%) removes the right to tint the front side windows; side mirrors on both sides required

rear.note: same as back side; side mirrors on each side required (§ 12-503(b-5))

tint.dualMirrors: Any vehicle with a treated window to the rear of the driver's seat must have a side mirror on each side (§ 12-503(b-5)).
tint.certificateOrSticker: Medical exemption vehicles need distinctive plates or plate stickers under § 3-412(k); installers must keep a copy of the physician's statement.

medicalExemption.text: Owner (or household member transported) with a medical disease requiring shielding from the sun (e.g., lupus, porokeratosis, TBI light sensitivity, albinism) needs a certified statement from an Illinois-licensed physician, carried in the vehicle, renewed every 4 years, copy sent to the Secretary of State; vehicle must have distinctive plates/stickers (§ 3-412(k)). Exempts windshield (a) and front side (a-5) rules.

penalty.text: Petty offense, fine $50 to $500; second or subsequent: Class C misdemeanor, fine $100 to $500; court orders windows brought into compliance.

tint.lastAmended: P.A. 103-32, eff. 1-1-24 (dealer test-drive rule); tint numbers unchanged
quotes: a nonreflective tinted film may be used along the uppermost portion of the windshield if such material does not extend more than 6 inches down from the top of the windshield.

On vehicles where none of the windows to the rear of the driver's seat are treated in a manner that allows less than 35% light transmittance, a nonreflective tinted film that allows at least 35% light transmittance, with a 5% variance

On vehicles where none of the windows to the rear of the driver's seat are treated in a manner that allows less than 30% light transmittance, a nonreflective tinted film that allows at least 50% light transmittance
Any motor vehicle with a window to the rear of the driver's seat treated in this manner shall be equipped with a side mirror on each side
shall be guilty of a petty offense and fined no less than $50 nor more than $500.

helmet.conditions: No motorcycle helmet requirement in the Illinois Vehicle Code

handheldPhone.fineText: max $75 first offense, $100 second, $125 third, $150 fourth+; aggravated (crash with great bodily harm or death): min $1,000 and Class A misdemeanor / Class 4 felony

studdedTires.season: banned except rural USPS letter carriers (Nov 15 - Apr 1) and certain disability/disabled-veteran plates in unincorporated areas

radarDetector.note: commercial vehicles over 10,001 lb banned federally (49 CFR 392.71)

underglow.rule: No red light visible from the front; flashing lights banned except as authorized; 'all other lighting or combination of lighting' not expressly authorized by the Code is prohibited; no smoked/tinted lens covers.

openQuestions: ilga.gov refused connections; statutes read from Wayback copies of the official ILCS pages (12-503: June 2026; 12-610.2: Aug 2026; 12-401: Oct 2025; 12-212: Nov 2025).

Rear/back side VLT: commonly reported as 35% for sedans and 'any' for MPVs, but § 12-503 sets no direct numeric rear limit - it conditions front tint on the rear windows. Recorded as 'any' with that condition.
Helmet: 'none' based on absence of a helmet requirement; no single cite to quote.
